content: In the opening inquiry of section 1 (the mental form), as paraphrased by Melvin-Koushki, Ibn Turka argues that philosophers hold absolute existence to be the most comprehensive concept, but it is relativized by its opposite, absolute nonexistence; every positive category is twinned with its negative inversion. The sole exception is waḥda, oneness, which cannot be so relativized, so the One alone is all-encompassing; the concept of number is the fountainhead of all the sciences.
